title: Group Think, Bias and Board Personalities
summary: The cognitive and social traps that undermine board decisions, the board personalities that distort discussion, and practical counter-measures the chair and directors can use.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: The cognitive and social traps that undermine board decisions, the board personalities that distort discussion, and practical counter-measures the chair and directors can use.
Learning Objectives: Recognise the warning signs of group think and common decision biases
Identify difficult board behaviours and how the chair should respond
Apply practical techniques to counter bias in board decisions
Syllabus: Group think, framing, availability and motivated blindness
Decision traps: time pressure, short horizons and isolation
Board personalities: the dominator, the silent director, the absentee and the box-ticker
Counter-measures: devil's advocate, anonymous polling and options before advocacy
Intended Audience: Chairs, non-executive and independent directors and board committee members
Executive directors and senior managers who present to or sit on the board
Company secretaries and heads of governance responsible for board processes and evaluation
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No prior governance training is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Corporate Governance Principles for Banks (2015)
Amy C. Edmondson, The Fearless Organization: Creating Psychological Safety in the Workplace (2018)
Olivier Sibony, You're About to Make a Terrible Mistake! How Biases Distort Decision-Making (2020)
